jobs.title: Principal BESS Engineer, Procurement & Performance | Energy
jobs.description:
As a Principal BESS Engineer , you will lead technical and commercial advisory services for utility-scale battery energy storage systems across development, procurement, contracting, delivery and operation. The role is particularly focused on Owner's Engineer and procurement engagements, where clients need clear advice on how a BESS should be sized, specified, evaluated and contracted to achieve its intended duty over its operating life. You will bring the technical depth to understand the system and the commercial judgement to translate that understanding into bankable requirements, meaningful bid comparisons and practical risk allocation.
You will work with clients to define the duty profile and performance basis for a project, develop Principal's requirements and technical schedules, assess OEM and integrator proposals, support tender evaluations and negotiate key performance and warranty provisions. This includes net power and usable energy, state-of-charge operating windows, round-trip efficiency, auxiliary consumption, availability, degradation, cycling and throughput, augmentation, response performance, reactive-power capability, environmental derating, warranties, acceptance tests and long-term service obligations. You will also support detailed design reviews, factory and site testing, commissioning and performance verification.
The common thread is being able to connect technology, contracts and lifecycle value. You will identify where apparently attractive offers rely on different assumptions, exclusions or operating limits, explain the consequences clearly, and help clients make decisions that remain robust after contract award. The role will suit a BESS specialist who is equally comfortable interrogating a technical proposal, leading a commercial discussion and coordinating the wider electrical, civil, fire, grid and operational interfaces.
How you’ll make a difference:
- Lead BESS Owner's Engineer and technical advisory engagements across feasibility, procurement, contracting, design, construction, commissioning and operation.
- Establish the BESS sizing and performance basis using the intended dispatch duty, grid requirements, site climate, operating strategy, reliability requirements and lifecycle objectives.
- Prepare and review Principal's requirements, technical schedules and guarantees covering net power, usable energy, round-trip efficiency, availability, auxiliary consumption, degradation, augmentation, throughput, response performance and reactive-power capability.
- Lead tender evaluations and normalise competing offers by interrogating assumptions, exclusions, operating limits, warranted curves, design margins, augmentation strategies, lifecycle costs and technical risks.
- Support contract negotiations on performance guarantees, test and acceptance methods, warranties, liquidated damages and remedies, scope interfaces, long-term service obligations, operations and maintenance, and augmentation responsibilities.
- Review BESS architecture and interfaces across cells, modules, racks, containers, battery management systems, energy management or plant control systems, power conversion systems, medium-voltage systems, thermal management, fire safety and the grid connection; coordinate specialists and mentor team members.
To be successful in this role, you will be an experienced BESS engineer or technical advisor with a demonstrated record in utility-scale battery projects and a strong understanding of both technical performance and commercial delivery. You may have developed this experience with an owner, developer, OEM, system integrator, EPC contractor, lender, investor or engineering consultancy.
You will be known for your ability to move confidently between system sizing, technical specifications, vendor proposals and contract schedules. You will understand that BESS offers cannot be compared reliably without aligning duty, system boundaries, ambient conditions, degradation assumptions, augmentation strategy, warranty limits, test methods and the definition of net performance. Experience supporting competitive procurements and contract negotiations will be central to success in this role.
You will know your way around a BESS project, from cells and racks through battery management systems, thermal management, power conversion systems, energy management or plant control systems, medium-voltage systems and the grid connection. You will understand how design, safety, site conditions, operating strategy and contractual obligations interact over the project life. One of your strengths will be knowing where detailed specialist input is required and coordinating the right technical and commercial contributors to reach a defensible client recommendation.
The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes, you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.
The qualities that help you thrive:
- Significant experience (8+ years) in the energy sector, including substantial hands-on experience with utility-scale BESS projects across development, procurement, delivery or operation.
- A background and experience of working in either / or a combination of consulting, developer, OEM, integrator or EPC industries.
- Strong capability in BESS sizing and operating-duty definition, including power and energy requirements, AC and DC boundaries, state-of-charge windows, duration, C-rate, cycling, throughput, degradation and augmentation.
- Detailed understanding of BESS performance criteria and guarantees, including net power, usable energy, round-trip efficiency, auxiliary consumption, availability, response, thermal derating, degradation, warranty limits and acceptance testing.
- Demonstrated experience preparing or reviewing procurement documentation, evaluating and normalising bids, undertaking technical due diligence, assessing departures and supporting commercial negotiations.
- Sound understanding of BESS technology and interfaces across cells, modules and racks, battery management systems, power conversion systems, energy management or plant control systems, medium-voltage balance of plant, grid connection, thermal management and fire safety.
- Experience with factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, capacity or efficiency testing, and verification of contractual performance requirements is highly regarded.
- Commercial acumen and the ability to assess lifecycle value, risk allocation, warranties, performance remedies, long-term service agreements, operations and maintenance obligations, and augmentation strategy.
- Strong client engagement and communication skills, with the ability to advise, influence and build trusted relationships across technical, procurement, commercial and executive teams.
- Either registered, or working towards professional registration, on the National Engineering Register in Australia (such as RPEV or RPEQ), ideally supported by Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status or equivalent international accreditation.
- A bachelor degree in electrical engineering, power systems or another engineering discipline relevant to battery energy storage systems.
Why you’ll love working with us
- Flexible work arrangements available, aligned with the market and client facing role requirements
- Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave per year
- Volunteer and representation leave
- Flex public holidays – swap Easter or other holidays for ones that suit you better

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?
We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.
Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

You will also support detailed design reviews, factory and site testing, commissioning and performance verification.
The common thread is being able to connect technology, contracts and lifecycle value. You will identify where apparently attractive offers rely on different assumptions, exclusions or operating limits, explain the consequences clearly, and help clients make decisions that remain robust after contract award. The role will suit a BESS specialist who is equally comfortable interrogating a technical proposal, leading a commercial discussion and coordinating the wider electrical, civil, fire, grid and operational interfaces.
How you’ll make a difference:
- Lead BESS Owner's Engineer and technical advisory engagements across feasibility, procurement, contracting, design, construction, commissioning and operation.
- Establish the BESS sizing and performance basis using the intended dispatch duty, grid requirements, site climate, operating strategy, reliability requirements and lifecycle objectives.
- Prepare and review Principal's requirements, technical schedules and guarantees covering net power, usable energy, round-trip efficiency, availability, auxiliary consumption, degradation, augmentation, throughput, response performance and reactive-power capability.
- Lead tender evaluations and normalise competing offers by interrogating assumptions, exclusions, operating limits, warranted curves, design margins, augmentation strategies, lifecycle costs and technical risks.
- Support contract negotiations on performance guarantees, test and acceptance methods, warranties, liquidated damages and remedies, scope interfaces, long-term service obligations, operations and maintenance, and augmentation responsibilities.
- Review BESS architecture and interfaces across cells, modules, racks, containers, battery management systems, energy management or plant control systems, power conversion systems, medium-voltage systems, thermal management, fire safety and the grid connection; coordinate specialists and mentor team members.
To be successful in this role, you will be an experienced BESS engineer or technical advisor with a demonstrated record in utility-scale battery projects and a strong understanding of both technical performance and commercial delivery. You may have developed this experience with an owner, developer, OEM, system integrator, EPC contractor, lender, investor or engineering consultancy.
You will be known for your ability to move confidently between system sizing, technical specifications, vendor proposals and contract schedules. You will understand that BESS offers cannot be compared reliably without aligning duty, system boundaries, ambient conditions, degradation assumptions, augmentation strategy, warranty limits, test methods and the definition of net performance. Experience supporting competitive procurements and contract negotiations will be central to success in this role.
You will know your way around a BESS project, from cells and racks through battery management systems, thermal management, power conversion systems, energy management or plant control systems, medium-voltage systems and the grid connection. You will understand how design, safety, site conditions, operating strategy and contractual obligations interact over the project life. One of your strengths will be knowing where detailed specialist input is required and coordinating the right technical and commercial contributors to reach a defensible client recommendation.
The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes, you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.
The qualities that help you thrive:
- Significant experience (8+ years) in the energy sector, including substantial hands-on experience with utility-scale BESS projects across development, procurement, delivery or operation.
- A background and experience of working in either / or a combination of consulting, developer, OEM, integrator or EPC industries.
- Strong capability in BESS sizing and operating-duty definition, including power and energy requirements, AC and DC boundaries, state-of-charge windows, duration, C-rate, cycling, throughput, degradation and augmentation.
- Detailed understanding of BESS performance criteria and guarantees, including net power, usable energy, round-trip efficiency, auxiliary consumption, availability, response, thermal derating, degradation, warranty limits and acceptance testing.
- Demonstrated experience preparing or reviewing procurement documentation, evaluating and normalising bids, undertaking technical due diligence, assessing departures and supporting commercial negotiations.
- Sound understanding of BESS technology and interfaces across cells, modules and racks, battery management systems, power conversion systems, energy management or plant control systems, medium-voltage balance of plant, grid connection, thermal management and fire safety.
- Experience with factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, capacity or efficiency testing, and verification of contractual performance requirements is highly regarded.
- Commercial acumen and the ability to assess lifecycle value, risk allocation, warranties, performance remedies, long-term service agreements, operations and maintenance obligations, and augmentation strategy.
- Strong client engagement and communication skills, with the ability to advise, influence and build trusted relationships across technical, procurement, commercial and executive teams.
- Either registered, or working towards professional registration, on the National Engineering Register in Australia (such as RPEV or RPEQ), ideally supported by Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) status or equivalent international accreditation.
- A bachelor degree in electrical engineering, power systems or another engineering discipline relevant to battery energy storage systems.

- Volunteer and representation leave

jobs.title: Procurement & SCM Lead
jobs.description:
Position Overview:
AECOM is seeking an experienced Procurement & Supply Chain Management (SCM) Lead to provide programme-level oversight of procurement, manufacturing, logistics, inspection, and delivery activities across a large-scale hybrid renewable energy programme. The role is responsible for maintaining end-to-end supply chain visibility, identifying risks to critical-path equipment and materials, and driving mitigation and recovery actions to support programme delivery objectives.
The position serves as the primary interface for supply chain monitoring and escalation across project packages, ensuring timely reporting of procurement and logistics risks while supporting informed decision-making by programme leadership and the Client.
Key Responsibilities:
Procurement & Supply Chain Governance
- Establish and maintain consolidated programme-wide visibility of procurement, manufacturing, factory acceptance testing (FAT), inspection status, dispatch, and delivery activities.
- Develop and maintain supply chain reporting frameworks, dashboards, and performance metrics.
- Monitor package-level procurement progress against project schedules and critical milestones.

Risk Identification & Mitigation
- Identify long-lead equipment and critical path supply chain risks impacting programme delivery.
- Assess risks associated with vendor capacity, manufacturing performance, transportation constraints, preservation requirements, equipment damage, and replacement lead times.
- Develop mitigation recommendations and recovery strategies for emerging risks.

Logistics & Expediting Management
- Coordinate expediting and recovery actions with package SCM teams, contractors, OEMs, and project leadership.
- Monitor transportation, customs clearance, warehousing, and site delivery performance.
- Escalate logistics bottlenecks and supply chain disruptions affecting project schedules.

Inspection & Manufacturing Coordination
- Interface with quality and inspection teams regarding manufacturing progress, inspection schedules, FAT readiness, and release status.
- Coordinate procurement and manufacturing updates to ensure alignment with project schedule requirements.
- Support readiness assessments for critical equipment deliveries and installation activities.

Reporting & Stakeholder Management
- Prepare regular reports highlighting procurement status, delivery performance, and key supply chain risks.
- Communicate schedule impacts arising from procurement delays, transportation restrictions, material shortages, and critical spare requirements.
- Provide factual delivery records and evidence-based reporting to support commercial evaluations and programme decision-making.

Programme Support
- Collaborate with planning, construction, quality, and package management teams to ensure integrated programme delivery.
- Support programme leadership in identifying recovery opportunities and supply chain optimization initiatives.
- Contribute to executive reviews, risk workshops, and programme governance meetings.
Minimum Qualification and Experience:
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Logistics, Business Administration, or related discipline.
- Professional certifications in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or Project Management are desirable.
- Minimum 10+ years of experience in procurement, supply chain management, logistics, or project delivery environments.
- Experience on large-scale infrastructure, renewable energy, power, transmission, or EPC projects preferred.
- Proven experience managing critical equipment procurement and international logistics activities.
Preferred Attributed:
- Strong understanding of procurement lifecycle management.
- Expertise in supply chain risk assessment and mitigation.
- Knowledge of manufacturing, FAT, inspection, logistics, and transportation processes.
- Experience with EPC, OEM, and contractor management environments.
- Strong analytical, reporting, and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple project packages.
- Excellent communication, coordination, and problem-solving capabilities.
- Advanced proficiency in project controls and reporting systems.

Preferred Experience:
- Utility-scale Solar Projects.
- Wind Energy Projects.
- Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
- Large Infrastructure and Energy Programs.
- Multi-contractor EPC delivery environments.
- International procurement and logistics operations.

At AECOM , we are currently recruiting for a Construction Risk Manager-Rail projects to join our Dublin office.
The Construction Risk Manager-Rail projects projects provides strategic leadership and oversight of risk management activities across the programme, ensuring a proactive and robust approach to identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that may impact project delivery, compliance, or organisational reputation. Working closely with executive leadership, delivery teams, and external stakeholders, the Risk Manager ensures that risk considerations are fully integrated into planning and execution activities. jobs.title: Program Risk Manager
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a  Program Risk Manager to join our team. This position is based on-site, out of  Mississauga.  We are seeking professionals to join our team to help us build one of the most advanced, sustainable and passenger-friendly airports in the world.
Major Responsibilities:
Reporting to the Risk Management Practice Lead, this position will be responsible for implementing a risk management program to support successful delivery of our client’s infrastructure development program in the Greater Toronto Area.  As an industry leader in program management and construction management for large capital programs, AECOM oversees activities ranging from planning, coordination, scheduling, and cost control, to design, construction, and commissioning. From concept through completion, we provide necessary technical and administrative services to help our clients meet their program objectives. We function as an extension of our clients’ staff, protecting their interests as our own.
The Program Risk Manager will be responsible for the delivery of risk management services to Client’s Infrastructure development program and projects.
Essential functions of the job include:
- Developing and implementing program and/or project risk management plans.
- Verifying and ensuring that agreed program and/or project Risk Management Plans are implemented by the project teams.
- Facilitating regular risk workshops and maintaining a good working knowledge of the program and/or projects and related activities to inform risk assessment and management.
- Advising and assisting program and/or project teams in implementing appropriate risk treatment plans and communicating risks to avoid surprises with key stakeholders.
- Integrating program-wide risk data to inform and support program’s day-to-day management of risks, program and/or project assurance, and decision-making processes.
- Conducting project and program-level schedule risk workshops/reviews and Quantitative Schedule Risk Assessments (QSRA).
- Conducting project and program-level cost risk workshops/reviews and Quantitative Cost Risk Assessments (QCRA).
- Providing periodic, accurate, and reliable risk reporting including performance trends and identifying items for management escalation.
- Creating and reporting regular leadership and executive level briefing papers to summarize key risks and mitigations as well as risk performance.
- Maintaining a program-wide register of identified and/or emergent risks and opportunities for use on future projects.
Minimum Requirements:
In order to be considered for this position, candidates must possess, at a very minimum:
- No less than a University Degree in project management, quantity surveying, engineering or related discipline plus 10 years of experience in development and implementation of risk management practices, risk identification, risk mitigation, and strategies on large construction projects/programs, including 2 years in leadership.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experienced in the facilitation of risk workshops and comfortable coordinating large groups of stakeholders.

- Familiarity and experience in the application of Quantitative Risk Analysis (QRA) techniques and tools.

- Experience using Enterprise Risk Management tools, for example, Active Risk Manager (ARM)

- Experience in the delivery of risk management activities and deliverables within a program/project lifecycle including support of investment decisions and milestone-based assurance reviews.

- Demonstrated understanding of the interfaces between risk management and other program/project management process areas, i.e. cost and schedule planning and control, change management, quality management, reporting, and commercial management.

- Understanding of various traditional and alternative contracting strategies and associated risks

- Experience working in the Engineering, Procurement and Construction advisory environment, specifically in the development of public infrastructure or other industrial projects.

- Effective verbal and written communications, and facilitation skills.

- Collaborative working style and behaviours, able to influence and engage stakeholders in managing risks.

- Ability to prioritize and manage multiple consulting engagements.

- Certified Risk Management Lead (CRM) or similar designation

- Membership of a professional body an asset (e.g. AACE, PMI)
This position requires work on-site/out of the office 5 days a week.
This position is for a replacement position.

jobs.title: Contracts and Procurement Manager – Transmission Line and Substation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose
Administer project contracts and monitor procurement activities to protect the Client's contractual and commercial interests, including variations, claims, extension of time, RA bills, BOQ control and contractor compliance.
Key Responsibilities
- Review contract conditions, technical scope, BOQ, payment terms, milestones and contractor obligations.
- Establish contract-administration procedures, correspondence protocols and contractual registers.
- Monitor compliance with contractual notices, securities, insurance, warranties and statutory obligations.
- Review variation proposals, change requests and scope-deviation submissions.
- Assess contractor claims for additional cost and extension of time in coordination with planning and technical teams.
- Verify claim entitlement, causation, substantiation, records and contractual notice compliance.
- Review RA bills, milestone invoices, quantity measurements, material reconciliation and supporting documentation.
- Recommend payment certification, withholding or recovery based on verified contractual performance.
- Maintain variation, claim, EOT, payment, guarantee, insurance and contractual correspondence registers.
- Monitor procurement schedules, vendor approvals, manufacturing progress, inspection, dispatch and delivery of critical materials and equipment.
- Review vendor and subcontractor compliance with approved specifications and contractual requirements.
- Support commercial negotiations and preparation of recommendations to the Client.
- Identify potential contractual exposures and recommend mitigation or dispute-avoidance measures.
- Support contract close-out, final account settlement, completion certification and release of contractual securities.
- Ensure commercial assessments are evidence-based and supported by contemporaneous project records.

Key Deliverables
- Contract-administration plan.
- Variation and change-control register.
- Claim and EOT assessment reports.
- RA bill and payment-certification recommendations.
- Procurement and expediting dashboard.
- Commercial-risk register.
- Final account and contract close-out report.
Minimum Qualification and Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quantity Surveying, Construction Management or equivalent.
- Minimum 10 years of contract administration experience in major infrastructure or power projects.
- Experience in EPC, item-rate, turnkey or FIDIC-based contracts.
- Knowledge of variations, claims, extension of time, payment certification and dispute avoidance.
- Familiarity with transmission line, substation and HVDC equipment procurement.
The position will be site-based at Khavda or Surat and may require travel between project locations, contractor offices, manufacturing facilities and client offices.
The successful candidate will work within a multidisciplinary AECOM Energy team supporting the safe and successful delivery of major HVDC and transmission infrastructure projects.

jobs.title: Procurement Manager - Rail & Transit
jobs.description:
AECOM Mississauga is seeking a Construction Management Procurement Lead to join our team for a newly created role.
About the Role
- We are seeking an experienced Construction/Procurement Manager, responsible for monitoring the procurement of construction, materials, equipment, and services by the contractor for adherence to contractual requirements to promote optimal value, risk allocation, and delivery outcomes.

- The ideal candidate will bring deep construction procurement process knowledge, especially in heavy civil, rail, and transit infrastructure, and be skilled in scoping subcontractor packages, the request for quotation process, understanding construction means and methods, and leveraging local market conditions to provide input into strategic sourcing decisions.

Responsibilities:
- Procurement Strategy:  Focussing on construction methodologies and sequencing, support the development and implementation of procurement strategies by the contractor which ensures the owner's interest in terms of value for money are protected while balancing factors such as timely delivery of the project, local capabilities, market capacity, and adherence to technical requirements.

- Procurement Process : monitor the contractor’s procurement process including supplier prequalification, scope definition, request for quotation issuance, bid evaluation, subcontract formation, and award recommendation.

- Supplier Negotiation:  Review pricing, contractual terms, and delivery schedules of subcontractors proposed by the contractor to assess alignment with contractual requirements, value for money principles and project timelines.

- Supplier Relationship & Market Engagement : Build and maintain strong relationships with the Contractor and supply chain to promote transparent communication and collaboration. Facilitate and participate in vendor days, market-engagement sessions, and supply-chain outreach activities with the Contractor to test capacity, encourage competition, and support value-for-money outcomes .

- Contract Management:  Reviewing contracts, change orders, and submittals to assess all procurement activities for alignment with project requirements.

- Issue Resolution:  Ability to work cooperatively with the contractor and internal stakeholders to manage and resolve any issues related to subcontracting and suppliers to prevent project delays.

-
Minimum Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.

- Minimum of 8 years of experience in procurement and supply chain management, with additional  experience in construction management.

Preferred Qualifications
- Ideally of 15 years of experience in construction management with additional experience in procurement and supply chain management, or a related field, with ideally 3 years in a managerial or supervisory role.

- Master's degree (e.g., MBA) is preferred but not required.

- Professional certifications such as Professional Engineer, Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM), Certified Purchasing Manager (CPM), and certifications in Construction Management are highly desirable.

- Excellent, analytical, negotiation and networking skills.

- Demonstrated ability to balance commercial acumen with technical insight in construction procurement.

- Conscientious, process oriented, and self-motivated

- Prior Market Engagement Experience is preferred.

Measure of Success
- Based on the ability for the individual to have a strong understanding of the design and construction of the project and ensure the project’s procurement and subcontracting strategies balances cost, schedule, quality, and value for money .

- Successful leadership of and collaboration with multidisciplinary team to achieve project milestones and deliverables.
- Sponsorship for Canadian employment authorization is not available for this position

jobs.title: Vice President, Global Growth Director – Defense Prime/OEM Facilities & Vertical Construction
jobs.description:
Vice President, Global Growth Director – Defense Prime/OEM Facilities & Vertical Construction
This is a high-impact leadership role within AECOM's Design Practice, responsible for defining and executing the US strategy for engagement with Defense Primes / OEM clients as it pertains to vertical construction, facilities delivery, and architectural and engineering design. This includes manufacturing and final assembly facilities, hangars and MRO facilities, training facilities, SCIF/SAPF and other ICD 705-compliant secure facilities, and program office space delivered at Defense Primes / OEM sites and government installations.
The position carries accountability for client relationships, growth strategy, pipeline development, capture, and delivery performance across AECOM’s Design practice. It combines strategic leadership with hands-on account execution to drive growth, strengthen client partnerships, and deliver consistent performance.
The primary role focuses on the U.S. market, but will also involve interaction with other AECOM regions including the UK, Continental Europe, Middle East, and Australia/New Zealand. This role is focused on Defense Primes / OEM clients (Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, BAE, RTX, etc.) — candidates with hands-on experience delivering vertical construction and facilities projects for these clients, at their own sites or at government-owned/contractor-operated facilities, will be looked upon most favorably. A background that spans a role with defense Primes / OEMs, followed by a career in A&E vertical construction delivery, is an ideal profile for this position.
This position will report to the AECOM’s Global Design Practice SVP, Head of Strategy & Growth, and will work closely with our US DOW Team and global defense leaders across the company.
We welcome applications from candidates who are already performing in a similar role, as well as those who have the experience, capability, and ambition to take the next logical step in their career progression into this position.
- Candidates must have a background in architecture, engineering, or a related A/E discipline with direct delivery experience on vertical construction projects (e.g., building design, building engineering, planning, or program/construction management) for Defense Primes / OEM clients — pure IT, cybersecurity, digital systems integration, or general business development backgrounds without hands-on A&E design or delivery experience will not meet the qualifications for this role.
- BA/BS +20 years’ experience or equivalent, including 4 years of leadership experience
- Due to the nature of the work, U.S. citizenship is required
- Proven experience working with Defense Primes / OEM clients and US DOW agencies on facilities and vertical construction programs (e.g., manufacturing, and final assembly facilities, hangars and MRO facilities, training facilities, SCIF/SAPF facilities, barracks)
- Commercial knowledge of the Defense Primes / OEM clients industry in relation to infrastructure needs, contracts, fees, and industry needs
- Leadership experience operating across geographies and multidisciplinary teams
- Demonstrated success leading accounts, complex pursuits, and multi-region delivery

Preferred background:
- Commercially astute, with executive stakeholder engagement skills
- Industrial background & experience in advanced manufacturing
- Direct project experience on Weapon System Bed downs, SCIF/SAPF or other ICD 705-compliant facilities, training facilities, hangars, MRO facilities, final assembly buildings, or program office space delivered for Defense Primes / OEM clients
- Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position

This role is focused on Defense Primes / OEM clients (Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, BAE, RTX, etc.) — candidates with hands-on experience delivering vertical construction and facilities projects for these clients, at their own sites or at government-owned/contractor-operated facilities, will be looked upon most favorably. A background that spans a role with defense Primes / OEMs, followed by a career in A&E vertical construction delivery, is an ideal profile for this position.
This position will report to the AECOM’s Global Design Practice SVP, Head of Strategy & Growth, and will work closely with our US DOW Team and global defense leaders across the company.
We welcome applications from candidates who are already performing in a similar role, as well as those who have the experience, capability, and ambition to take the next logical step in their career progression into this position.

- Due to the nature of the work, U.S. citizenship is required
- Proven experience working with Defense Primes / OEM clients and US DOW agencies on facilities and vertical construction programs (e.g., manufacturing, and final assembly facilities, hangars and MRO facilities, training facilities, SCIF/SAPF facilities, barracks)
- Commercial knowledge of the Defense Primes / OEM clients industry in relation to infrastructure needs, contracts, fees, and industry needs
- Leadership experience operating across geographies and multidisciplinary teams
- Demonstrated success leading accounts, complex pursuits, and multi-region delivery

Preferred background:
- Commercially astute, with executive stakeholder engagement skills
- Industrial background & experience in advanced manufacturing
- Direct project experience on Weapon System Bed downs, SCIF/SAPF or other ICD 705-compliant facilities, training facilities, hangars, MRO facilities, final assembly buildings, or program office space delivered for Defense Primes / OEM clients

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Program Manager to lead capital programs across Philadelphia. The role of a program manager is to ensure facilities are planned, designed, and delivered on time, within budget, and to quality standards.
The Program Manager will serve as the client’s trusted advisor and owner’s representative, leading a multi-disciplinary team and managing a portfolio of projects from planning through closeout.
This person will be responsible for but not limited to the following:
- Lead the integrated program management of a multi-project portfolio, establishing consistent processes, controls, and reporting.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for the client, providing strategic guidance, issue resolution, and decision support.
- Align program delivery with stakeholder priorities, funding constraints, and expected outcomes.
- Develop and maintain program-level plans, master schedules, and budget baselines; implement change control and variance analysis.
- Forecast cashflow and manage contingencies; ensure compliance with funding and reporting requirements.
- Coordinate sequencing, phasing, and risk-adjusted scheduling to minimize facility disruption.
- Support procurement strategies (CM/GC, design-bid-build, design-build), RFP development, evaluation, and award recommendations.
- Administer contracts and change orders; manage claims and dispute avoidance with fair, transparent processes.
- Lead public outreach and community meetings, ensuring transparency and responsiveness to school and neighborhood needs.
- Prepare executive dashboards, board-ready reports, and presentations.
Minimum Requirements
- BA/BS plus eight years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
- US Drivers License.

Preferred Requirements
- Professional certifications: PMP, CCM, PE, AIA, or equivalent.
- Experience delivering capital programs in Pennsylvania or the City of Philadelphia, with knowledge of local codes, permitting, and public procurement practices.
- Familiarity with union environments, prevailing wage, and workforce participation goals (MBE/WBE/DBE).
- Experience with occupied-facilties construction, phasing, and environmental considerations (e.g., abatement coordination, IAQ).
- Must meet all client background clearance requirements (e.g., criminal history, abuse clearance, and FBI fingerprinting, as applicable).
- Ability to attend evening or weekend community meetings if/when required.
- Sponsorship is not available for this position.
- Relocation is not available for this position.

jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a detail-oriented Labor Compliance Specialist to review contractor Certified Payroll Records (CPRs) for compliance with California public works labor laws to work remotely or in Los Angeles, CA . This role supports transportation infrastructure projects and ensures contractors and subcontractors comply with prevailing wage requirements, apprenticeship regulations, and certified payroll reporting standards .
The ideal candidate has experience with California Department of Industrial Relations (DIR) requirements , public works labor compliance , and reviewing certified payroll submissions for accuracy and regulatory compliance.
Key Responsibilities
- Review contractor and subcontractor Certified Payroll Records (CPRs) for accuracy and compliance with California prevailing wage laws.
- Verify proper classification of workers , wage rates, overtime calculations, and fringe benefit reporting.
- Confirm compliance with DIR Public Works requirements and applicable wage determinations.
- Identify and flag labor compliance violations , such as underpayment, misclassification, or incomplete payroll submissions.
- Communicate discrepancies and required corrections to contractors and project management teams.
- Track payroll submissions and maintain organized compliance records.
- Ensure adherence to apprenticeship utilization and reporting requirements when applicable.
- Support audits or documentation requests related to labor compliance.
Minimum Requirements
- BA/BS + 4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
- US citizenship is a requirmeent for this role.

- 4+ years of experience in California public works labor compliance or certified payroll review.
- Strong knowledge of California prevailing wage laws and DIR reporting requirements .
- Experience reviewing Certified Payroll Records (CPRs) and Statement of Compliance forms.
- Familiarity with transportation or infrastructure public works projects.
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify wage or reporting discrepancies.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Experience with LCPtracker, Elation Systems, or similar labor compliance software .

AECOM  is a leader in the global data center consulting industry with robust teams in the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.  In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with our teams around the world on high-profile, fast-paced data center projects for global clients.  This is a hands-on, client-facing role with an opportunity for upward career mobility.

We are seeking an experienced Program Manager to play a critical leadership role within the AECOM US Data Center Practice. This role operates at the intersection of business development, client management, and project delivery, ensuring that client pursuits are competitive, programs are executed efficiently, and financial and operational objectives are achieved.
The Program Manager will partner closely with executive leadership, design directors, client account managers, and discipline leaders to support revenue growth, client satisfaction, and operational excellence across hyperscale and colocation data center programs.
This position is ideal for a highly organized, business-minded leader with deep experience in managing complex A/E/C programs and supporting major proposal pursuits.
Key Responsibilities:
- Provide program-level leadership across multiple concurrent data center design projects
- Monitor program performance including schedule, budget, staffing, and risk
- Identify and resolve program-level constraints impacting delivery
- Ensure consistency of execution across multiple projects and clients
- Support Design Managers and Project Managers in maintaining successful delivery

- Proposal schedules and deliverable management
- Fee strategy coordination
- Staffing plans and resource alignment
- Executive review coordination
- Interview preparation and coaching
- Coordinate closely with Client Account Managers, and Technical Leaders
- Improve proposal processes, templates, and win strategies
- Support capture planning for strategic pursuits
- Serve as a key point of contact for strategic clients

- Participate in client meetings, presentations, and program reviews
- Support Client Account Managers in maintaining strong client relationships
- Help identify new opportunities within existing client programs
- Assist in managing client expectations and overall client experience
- ·Travel as needed for project-related activities such as client meetings and site visits.

- Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or related field plus eight (8) years of relevant experience, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
- Minimum 5+ years managing complex programs or major projects
- Experience supporting or leading proposal efforts
- Strong understanding of A/E/C project delivery process
- Excellent communication and leadership skills
- Strong business and financial acumen
- Ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities

- 10 plus years of relevant experience.
- Direct experience supporting data center projects
- Experience working with hyperscale or colocation clients
- Experience managing large multi-disciplinary design teams
- Experience with Design-Bid-Build and Design-Build delivery models
- PMP certification preferred
- Professional licensure (Architect, Engineer) is a plus but not required.

jobs.title: Senior Risk Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description
As a Senior Risk Manager, you will be responsible for implementing and advising on Risk Management solutions for AECOM’s major infrastructure projects across a broad range of sectors.
Working as part of the AECOM Integrated Programme Controls team, the Senior Risk Manager will need to be comfortable with engaging with senior stakeholders and customers. They will work closely with a range of internal, client and sub-contractor staff to develop an accurate understanding of risk exposure, implementing appropriate governance and supporting effective decision making.
You will be part of an established team of risk professionals supporting various capital projects across the UK with opportunities to support AECOM’s vast number of projects and programmes globally.
As a Senior Risk Consultant, you will have the following key accountabilities.
- Engage with project teams to ensure the effective implementation of risk management
- Provide direct risk management input to bids and proposals to secure new business
- Perform risk assurance checks to ensure the quality of project and programme risk management
- Communicate key project and programme risk management data to senior leaders
- Produce comprehensive risk reports for informed decision
- Coaching and mentoring staff in risk management best practice
- Facilitate identification, assessment and prioritisation of risks
- Develop robust Risk Registers, Risk Management Plans, and Risk Mitigation Plans
- Conduct Quantitative Risk Analysis (QCRA and QSRA), utilising techniques such as Monte-Carlo to establish project contingency levels.
- Ability to design and implement risk management frameworks for projects and programmes
- Support cost, scheduling, project controls and change management teams where appropriate.

If you're passionate about innovation and turning bold ideas into reality, AECOM welcomes you. Join our team, where we don't just construct infrastructure but also uplift communities and enhance lives. Why not give our AECOM page on LinkedIn a follow to stay updated on the impactful projects we're working on and see firsthand the difference we're making in the industry!
What we’re looking for?
As the ideal candidate you will have experience working within our primary markets along with having the following preferred experience and qualifications.
- You will be required to have 3+ years experience in risk management, with at least 2 years experience of risk management activities on high value projects.
- Bachelor’s Degree from a recognised and accredited university or hold a risk management qualification (MOR, APM Risk, IRM)
- Proven experience and excellent working knowledge gained in a multi-discipline project environment.
- Proficient in the use of Industry Risk Management tools (ARM, Xactium, RiskHive, Predict etc.)
- Demonstrable experience in conducting Quantitative Risk Analysis (QCRA & QSRA) using tools such as Safran, Primavera Risk Analyser, @risk..
- Competency in implementing Risk Management processes aligned with ISO31000, Institute of Risk Management, or Association of Project Management methodologies.
- Flexibility to travel and work in different sectors.
- Good people management and task facilitation skills.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
AECOM Canada is seeking a motivated and analytical Financial Analyst to join our Finance Development Program in a new position to be based in Markham, ON . This role is designed for recent graduates who are interested in building a career in finance, project accounting, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), and business operations.
Through a structured rotational experience, the successful candidate will gain exposure to financial planning, project financial management, internal controls, and operational finance processes while supporting some of Canada's largest infrastructure and professional services projects.
This role will work closely with Finance Managers, Project Accounting teams and FP&A professionals to help drive financial performance across AECOM 's Canadian businesses and provides a unique opportunity to develop technical, analytical, and business partnering skills while learning the fundamentals of project-based financial management.
What You Will Learn
Throughout the program, the Finance Graduate will gain practical experience in:
- Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
- Operational Finance & Business Partnering
- Working Capital Management
- Financial Forecasting & Budgeting
- Project Finance
- Business Intelligence & Data Analytics
- Executive Reporting
- Professional Services and Infrastructure Project Economics
- Internal Controls, Compliance & Governance

Key Responsibilities
Financial Planning & Analysis
- Support monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes.
- Assist with budgeting, forecasting, business planning, and outlook submissions.
- Develop and enhance management reports, dashboards, and financial analysis tools.
- Analyze financial and operational performance trends and provide actionable insights.
- Assist with automation initiatives and continuous process improvements using financial systems and reporting tools.
- Support ad hoc reporting, variance analysis, and special projects.

Project Accounting & Financial Operations
- Manage a portfolio of projects and support project financial administration activities.
- Assist Project Managers and Finance teams with project setup, maintenance, invoicing, and revenue recognition processes.
- Monitor project performance, profitability, backlog, unbilled receivables, and cash collection metrics.
- Support month-end close activities and project financial reviews.
- Learn project accounting fundamentals and gain exposure to the full project lifecycle from project setup through project closeout.

Finance Team Support
- Support Project Accounting Managers with recurring weekly and monthly processes.
- Assist with: - P&L Proforma reviews
- Consolidated percentage-of-completion reporting
- Accounts receivable and Unbilled reserve analysis
- ODC accrual reviews
- R18 and project financial review processes

- Prepare analysis and supporting schedules for management review.

Internal Controls, Compliance & Governance
- Participate in maintaining compliance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
- Support activities related to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance and internal control requirements.
- Assist with documenting and improving financial processes and controls.
- Contribute to ensuring accuracy, transparency, and accountability in financial reporting and business practices.
Required Qualifications
- Recent university graduate with a Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting or a related discipline.

Preferred Qualifications
- Working toward CPA designation or interest in pursuing CPA.
- Internship, co-op, or relevant work experience in finance, accounting, consulting, engineering, or professional services is an asset.

Preferred Skills & Competencies
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Advanced Excel skills and an aptitude for data analysis.
- Interest in financial modelling and business performance management.
- Well-developed interpersonal, presentation and communication skills including a proven ability to develop and maintain productive working relationships
- Strong attention to detail with a commitment to accuracy.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office; knowledge of AI and Business Intelligence tools.
- Relocation is not available for this position.
- Sponsorship for Canadian employment authorization is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

jobs.title: Program Analyst
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking an experienced Program Analyst to support our team in Detroit, Michigan .
The Program Analyst partners with Information Technology and Finance, Customer Service, and Operations business units to plan, track, and deliver technology initiatives with minimal direction and supervision. This role combines systems and applications expertise with business analysis, process improvement, project coordination, compliance, financial tracking, and document management.
The Program Analyst works directly with customers and stakeholders to define business requirements, improve existing systems and workflows, support project management systems, and maintain the accuracy and integrity of business and project data throughout the lifecycle.
Key Responsibilities
- Partner with business units and IT teams to define business requirements, application goals, functional requirements, and technical specifications.
- Support the configuration, enhancement, upgrade, deployment, integration, and maintenance of applications and systems.
- Support Project Managers with software rollouts, project scope, schedules, task estimates, deliverables, and project tracking.
- Analyze business processes and workflows; identify opportunities for improvement and perform fit-gap, cost-benefit, and ROI analyses.
- Serve as a liaison between software vendors, end users, IT staff, and business stakeholders to resolve issues and support effective solutions.

jobs.title: Procurement Specialist
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Procurement Specialist to work a hybrid schedule which is located in Sacramento, CA.
JOB SUMMARY:
This role will support the efficient execution for managing, preparing, and analyzing contracts and procurement agreements for CAHSR.
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Applies knowledge and utilization of both efficient procurement processes, market research, and good business management to ensure timely delivery of goods and services to the customer.
- Utilizes innovative cost and time efficient strategies in decision-making in the acquisition process.
- Formulates the contracting approach to be taken that will best satisfy the requirement. Determines the type of contract best suited to the requirement, developed by the appropriate special clauses and terms and conditions applicable to the solicitation.
- Performs cost and price analysis for all negotiations and supporting documentation for price fair and reasonableness determinations.
- Throughout the life of the A/E, supply, construction, information technology, utility and service contract, maintains liaison with the contractor to interpret contractual obligations and provide problem resolution under the direction of the Contract Manager.
- Coordinating with legal, finance, and other departments ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements
- Implementing contract management policies and procedures, and identifying areas for improvement
- Monitoring contract execution to ensure obligations are met, while maintaining detailed records of contract documents and communications
- Providing training and guidance on contract-related issues to teammates/staff
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders across departments to ensure contracts align with business objectives and risk tolerance.
- Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, as well as internal CAHSR policies and regulations.
- Under management’s supervision, coordinates review of developed customized contract drafts by stakeholders (i.e. Legal - based on associated risk, Risk Management & Insurance Services, Audit Services, Environmental Services, Safety, etc.) to mitigate risk.
- Under management’s supervision, reviews, modifies, and negotiates contract terms and conditions to mitigate risk.
- Prepares, maintains and reviews purchasing files, reports and price lists.  Prepares purchase orders and sends copies to suppliers and to departments originating requests.
- Actively aware of safety in day-to-day activities.
- Responds to customer and supplier inquiries about order status, changes, or cancellations in a timely manner supporting CAHSR needs.
- Under management’s supervision, compares prices, specifications, and delivery dates to determine the best acquisition method, while preparing all PreAward/PreSolicitation documentation.
- Tracks the status of requisitions, contracts, and orders.
- Contributes to the overall success of the AECOM and CAHSR office by performing all other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:
- BA/BS + 6 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS:
- Master’s Degree/Juris Doctorate
- FAC-C Professional, DAWIA Level II or III, or equivalent.
- Minimum five (5) years’ experience in contract management, the principles, contractual terms, pricing structures, pricing tools and data systems, negotiation, project support, finance, contracting, or proposals.
- Strong presentation skills and the ability to effectively communicate in writing and in person.
- Demonstrated well-developed organizational and time-management skills and proven ability to prioritize multiple demands and meet established deadlines and commitments.
- Demonstrated leadership skills as well as the ability to manage multiple priorities within strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: Senior Federal Invoice Compliance Specialist
jobs.location: City of Taguig, BONIFACIO STOPOVER, ph
jobs.description:
The role will support the Federal Procurement Team in ensuring subcontractor invoices, closeouts, and certified payrolls align with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements and subcontract terms.
-  Receive, review, and process subcontractor invoices, closeout documentation, and certified payrolls associated with federal subcontracts established by Federal Business Services (FBS) Subcontract Specialists.
- Review invoices, closeouts, and certified payroll submissions for compliance with subcontract terms, applicable FAR clauses, and federal contract requirements, including but not limited to payment, labor, and audit provisions.
- Validate invoicing supports allowable, allocable, and reasonable costs in accordance with contract type (e.g., cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, or fixed-price).
- Track, log, and monitor all incoming, approved, rejected, and outstanding invoices, closeouts, and certified payrolls for assigned job numbers to ensure timely review and resolution.
-  Coordinate and correspond with Project Managers, subcontractors/vendors, Accounts Payable, and internal compliance team members to resolve invoicing discrepancies, missing documentation, labor compliance issues, or payment delays.
- Ensure documentation supports Prompt Payment Act requirements and subcontract payment timing.
- Maintain organized, auditable electronic files and records in compliance with AECOM procedures and federal record-retention requirements.
- Support subcontract closeout activities, confirming submission and acceptance of all required financial, labor, and compliance documentation.
- Participate in and complete required Federal Business Services and compliance training.
- Manage full invoice, certified payroll, and closeout compliance responsibilities on large or complex federal projects independently
- Analyze issues and identify solutions using existing techniques, and propose approaches for novel issues
- Identify opportunities for process improvements, automation, or risk reduction and partner with team leadership to implement improvements.
Minimum Requirements
- Bachelor’s degree in accountancy or any related field of study
- Five (5) years or more of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
- Experience in supporting invoice verification, payment processing for US Federal Projects

jobs.title: Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
AECOM  is seeking for an experienced Compliance Specialist  for employment for full-time  on-site  support at Fort Bragg in North Carolina.

The responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Fully qualified scientist. Utilizes scientific principles, theories, practices and existing technologies to develop technical solutions to a wide range of difficult problems.
- Requires general familiarity within a broad field of scientific knowledge of reciprocal effects of the work upon other disciplines/fields.
- Interprets and records data, conducts analyses, compares findings to relevant studies and local, state, and federal regulations to ensure compliance.
- Works under only general direction. Independently determines and develops approach to solutions.
- Solves problems by use of combinations of standard procedures, modifications of standard procedures or methods developed in previous assignments.
- Participates in planning required to achieve prescribed objectives.
- Conducts analysis and investigation work obtained from a variety of sources.
- Participates in developing corrective measures and procedures. Formulates hypothesis, performs research and makes recommendation.
- The candidate shall be expected to perform on-site installation support tasks to help maintain compliance with the facilities’ Title V Air Operating permits and verify that emissions do not exceed air quality standards.
- The candidate will be required to assist installation Air Quality Program Managers with the collection of monthly recordkeeping, update quality assurance checklists, emission limit monitoring, and demonstrate compliance with Title V permit conditions.
Minimum Requirements:
- BA/BS + 2 Years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
- Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.
- In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background, medical and drug screening requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
- Must possess a valid driver’s license and clean driving record, will be required to drive to various site locations throughout Military base to do site inspections.
- Physically able, with or without an accommodation, to work in indoor and outdoor environments with uneven terrain and variable outdoor conditions.
- Frequently (more than 50% of workday) performing keyboard/mouse operations.  Often (25-50% of the workday) standing/walking, and operating vehicles.  Occasionally (10-25% of the workday) climbing stairs.  Rarely (less than 10% of the workday) lifting less than 50 pounds.
- This position will include wearing associated personal protective equipment including, but not limited to safety shoes/boots and hard hat.

Preferred Qualifications:
- 4+ years of experience in Army air quality management, air emissions inventories, operating permit compliance, New Source Performance Standards and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants compliance, New Source Review permitting, regulatory reporting, permit renewals, major source determination, refrigerant management, and air impact assessment under General Conformity and National Environmental Policy Act.
- Federal experience in air quality management, air emissions inventories, operating permit compliance, New Source Performance Standards and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants compliance, New Source Review permitting, regulatory reporting, permit renewals, major source determination, refrigerant management, and air impact assessment under General Conformity and National Environmental Policy Act.
- The candidate shall have knowledge and experience with Federal air quality environmental data management requirements, processes, and systems, to include, but not be limited to The Air Program Information Management System (APIMS) and the Air Conformity Applicability Model (ACAM).
- In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
- Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.
- Relocation Benefits are not available for this position.
